feature: One commander row — the play-style sentence, the mechanic gap, one Fit
note: Written at close-out, extended 2026-09-18. FIVE cells at two widths: both lanes, `/discover` under `Something new`, `/discover` searched to the catalogue's longest sentence, and `/commanders` searched to state 4. Both lanes are shot because the row is ONE component serving two populations and the whole ruling (D1) is that nothing on it may be read off ownership — so a sheet showing only one lane would photograph the ruling's easy half. `/discover` is where the price draws and `/commanders` is where it never does: every commander there is owned, and §7.4 row 5 unmounts the slot. State 4 IS forced, by searching a commander that draws it — and it had to be, because it is 5.7% of `/commanders` on this account, so both lane cells photograph `unplayed` and the state shipped through the whole feature unphotographed. The commander was found with `scripts/measure-gap-line.mts`; `noMechanics` is 3.5% of the catalogue and is still unforced, so it may not appear. What the sheet CANNOT show is the states matrix — that is `commander-row.test.tsx`'s job, 35 cases — nor the browser-measured figures, which are `probe:commander-row`'s. A picture proves the row rendered on the route; it does not prove a state.

shares.why: The point of the feature. Two routes, one row, and `check:shared` is what proves they converged rather than each growing a copy — which is exactly what `rec-card.tsx` and `discovery-row.tsx` were before this round.
